S1_incident_reporting.quote: Manufacturers shall report every thermal incident involving overheating, fire, injury, or property damage to the relevant regulator within 24 hours of becoming aware of it, with a written incident report and available investigation findings within 10 calendar days. They shall notify affected customers within 48 hours when an incident presents a potential safety risk to their model or installation, and provide updates when material new information becomes available.

S2_thermal_testing.quote: A failure rate of 5% is a regulatory action threshold, not an automatic prohibition on certification, sales, or installation. Manufacturers shall provide complete per-model results to the relevant regulator and to customers who buy or own that model, in clear, accessible form, and retain results for audit.

S3_remote_shutoff.quote: All newly manufactured home battery systems shall support remote emergency shut-off no later than 36 months after adoption of this standard. For units already installed on the adoption date, manufacturers shall provide a remote shut-off retrofit or an equivalent safe, documented alternative within six years, prioritizing units with known safety concerns.

S4_fire_suppression.quote: All newly manufactured home battery units shall include built-in fire suppression no later than 36 months after adoption of this standard.

S5_customer_disclosure.quote: When a model exceeds 8 confirmed thermal incidents per 100,000 installed units in any 12-month period, the manufacturer shall promptly notify the regulator and affected customers and provide supporting model-level data. The threshold shall trigger a regulator-led safety assessment, not an automatic recall; the regulator shall determine whether a recall or other proportionate measure is required based on model-specific evidence and risk.

document.section_notes: The final text makes the 5% S2 threshold a regulatory action trigger with no automatic sales stop, which shields Northwind's Hearth 10 (6.2%) and fails the answer key's sales-stop requirement. S5 sets 8/100k as a trigger for regulator assessment rather than a mandatory recall, which protects Halcyon's Ember 8 (9.9/100k), while S3 gives installed units six years for retrofit and S4 sets built-in suppression at 36 months. S1 is strong, with 24-hour reporting for all thermal incidents and 48-hour customer notice, and the document is signed by both parties.
